Agreed action items and owners; next meeting to review RA and benchmark results.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a quick roll call and then jump into the architecture and marketplace flow.
[00:08] Liam O'Neill: Hi, Liam here from OrionCloud, joining from Dublin.
[00:11] Priya Singh: Priya, SE on the Orion side.
[00:13] Markus Vogel: Markus, marketplace ops.
[00:15] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood, SE.
[00:17] Maya Kapoor: Maya from Product at Redwood.
[00:18] Avery Chen: Great. Quick agenda — Marketplace listing checklist, RA for private and hosted variants, SSO/SAML details, benchmark plan, and next steps. Any additions?
[00:28] Liam O'Neill: No that's good. We mainly want to make sure the listing supports both our managed and marketplace buying flows.
[00:33] Priya Singh: Also to confirm network connectivity patterns, like if customers want to use the VPC connector or opt for our hosted integration.
[00:40] Diego Ramos: Right, and we'll surface the two deployment archetypes in the RA — hosted (Redwood-managed) and private (customer VPC or Orion managed). We'll call out KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[00:49] Markus Vogel: On the marketplace side, we need metadata: 1-2 line descriptions, logo, screenshots, and a tech contact for the listing review.
[00:56] Avery Chen: We'll provide a template for that today in the follow-up.
[00:59] [01:05] -- Discussion: Reference Architecture --
[01:05] Diego Ramos: For the RA, we're proposing a diagram that shows three lanes: Redwood control plane (SaaS), Orion marketplace listing & procurement flow, and customer data plane (VPC/private). The tricky part is how we represent KV cache and persistent caches — sometimes the transcript or docs call it K-V cash, so apologies for the poor OCR stuff in the draft.
[01:25] Priya Singh: Yeah we've seen customers confused by the term KV cache, maybe add a quick glossary.
[01:29] Maya Kapoor: Good call. We'll include glossary notes. Also we'll include an explicit section for network egress and regional restrictions — data residency was called out by a few of your customers last quarter, right?
[01:38] Liam O'Neill: Correct, EU customers need the EU region listing, and we need to call that out in the RA and the marketplace metadata.
[01:45] Diego Ramos: For private deployments, the RA will show a connector pattern: Lightweight agent deployed in the customer's VPC that proxies requests to the model runtime or, for dedicated deployments, points to reserved capacity. We'll list required ports, certs, and KMS integration.
[01:58] [02:07] Priya Singh: For SSO, what does Redwood prefer? SAML or OIDC? Our marketplace handles SSO via SAML for vendor portals today.
[02:15] Avery Chen: We support both; SAML is fine. We'll need metadata endpoints and a contact to complete the SAML metadata exchange. Also we'll capture RBAC mapping (what roles map to Redwood roles).
[02:26] Markus Vogel: On our side the listing review needs a security contact and a SOC 2 statement, any certs to include?
[02:33] Maya Kapoor: Yes we'll attach SOC 2 type II summary and a link to our compliance pack. We'll also include how audit logs can be exported to the customer's SIEM via our events API.
[02:44] [03:05] -- Benchmarking & Performance --
[03:05] Diego Ramos: Ok on benchmarks — the primary ask from OrionCloud was throughput and p95 serving latency for a typical 512-token workload and also a 2048-token LLM flow. We'll propose a runbook: 1) synthetic load on hosted Redwood API, 2) run on dedicated reserved capacity config that matches Orion's expected offering, and 3) run on private VPC-connected deployment if customer wants.
[03:30] Liam O'Neill: We'll need cost estimates too, because our marketplace pricing page needs a rough unit cost to help customers compare.
[03:37] Diego Ramos: We'll include avg token cost and delta for dedicated vs hosted and also note quantization impacts — i.e., 4-bit vs 8-bit. Our Redwood Optimize suggestions will be in the RA appendix.
[03:49] Priya Singh: Slight transcription hiccup: you said \"quantization\" but the notes had \"quantization or quantization\" twice, not sure.
[03:55] Diego Ramos: Yep, apologies for the stutter, we'll clean it up in the RA.
[03:58] [04:10] -- Marketplace Listing Flow & Procurement --
[04:10] Markus Vogel: For procurement, our flow is: listing approved -> pricing & SKUs published -> onboarding slot for provisioning -> post-listing QA. We need a partner contact and provisioning API keys flow.
[04:23] Avery Chen: Redwood can expose provisioning keys via our partner portal, we can automate onboarding via a signed URL exchange. We'll document the API call sequence in the RA.
[04:33] Liam O'Neill: Are there rate limit or token quotas we should call out in the listing?
[04:38] Diego Ramos: Yes, we'll include default rate limits and a note that dedicated capacity can be purchased for higher TPS. Also mention burst policies and autoscaling.
[04:47] Maya Kapoor: And we'll include sample SDK snippets for provisioning and token rotation.
[04:51] [05:05] -- Security & Compliance --
[05:05] Priya Singh: A couple of customers insisted on KMS integration, e.g., using their own cloud KMS or HSM. How do we represent that?
[05:13] Diego Ramos: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS integrations; we'll call that out as an optional step in the private deployment RA. For hosted listings, we provide an encrypted-at-rest note plus options for dedicated with CMK.
[05:26] Liam O'Neill: Any concerns about audit logs and egress for regulated customers?
[05:30] Maya Kapoor: We'll show an audit log export path to the customer's S3 destination or SIEM, and recommend VPC peering for low-latency private flows.
[05:41] [06:00] -- Integration specifics (SSO/SAML) --
[06:00] Diego Ramos: For the SAML flow: we'll need Orion's IDP metadata and an endpoint for assertion consumer service (ACS). On our side we map groups to roles and provide SCIM for provisioning if required.
[06:13] Priya Singh: SCIM would be great, we can provision customers' teams automatically.
[06:16] Avery Chen: SCIM is optional but supported; Diego will send the SCIM spec snippet and attribute mappings.
[06:24] Diego Ramos: I'll also include a note about session timeout defaults and how to override per-tenant.
[06:30] [07:02] -- Demo & assets --
[07:02] Markus Vogel: For the marketplace listing preview we need screenshots and a short demo video (60-90s) highlighting the provision flow.
[07:12] Maya Kapoor: Redwood can produce a 90s walkthrough showing provisioning and metrics in the console; we'll need a contact to record.
[07:18] Liam O'Neill: Priya can help with a scripted demo.
[07:21] Priya Singh: Yep, happy to help.
[07:24] [07:30] -- Pricing & SKUs --
[07:30] Avery Chen: We'll propose SKUs: hosted per-token unit, dedicated reserved capacity monthly commit, and a private deployment enterprise license. We'll add example price bands for the marketplace.
[07:43] Liam O'Neill: Marketplace tends to display price tiers; can you provide a recommended default tiering?
[07:48] Maya Kapoor: We'll include three tiers with typical usage buckets and the expected p95 latency per tier as a selling point.
[07:58] [08:15] -- Bench run specifics --
[08:15] Diego Ramos: For the benchmark runbook: test vectors (1k prompts), baseline model variants (we'll list two open models and a Redwood-verified profile), expected sequence lengths, and a load generator config. We'll also record token-level cost.
[08:33] Priya Singh: For private customers we'd like to know the minimum infra footprint. Can you share a reference size?
[08:40] Diego Ramos: Yes — we'll include a reference architecture that maps requests per second to GPU types and memory needs — e.g., 8xA100 for X TPS at 512 tokens. We'll note that quantized models can run on smaller GPUs but with quality tradeoffs.
[08:58] [09:20] -- Questions from OrionCloud --
[09:20] Liam O'Neill: Question: if a client purchases via marketplace, can they choose a Redwood Dedicated instance pinned to them?
[09:29] Avery Chen: Yes, the procurement can route to a dedicated reservation allocation — we just need to wire the customer account to the reservation via the onboarding flow. We'll outline that in the RA and the listing integration notes.
[09:40] Priya Singh: And how do rollouts look? If a model update regresses quality, can customers pin older versions?
[09:45] Diego Ramos: Absolutely — our runtime supports model pinning and automatic fallback. We'll document the rollout and canary steps and tie them to the console's rollouts UI.
[09:57] [10:22] -- Minor transcription artifacts (noise) --
[10:22] Diego Ramos: Note the auto-transcript sometimes mangles product names, like 'Redwood Optimize' might read as 'red bud optimize' in the automated notes. We'll provide a cleaned RA PDF.
[10:34] [11:05] -- Timeline & gating criteria --
[11:05] Avery Chen: Proposed timeline: RA draft sent by 2026-07-23, marketplace assets by 2026-07-26, benchmark week of 2026-07-27, internal listing review by Orion 2026-07-30, and publish target 2026-08-10. Any blockers?
[11:21] Markus Vogel: Need to confirm legal checklist; we'll share onboarding window constraints.
[11:26] Liam O'Neill: Also need to validate regional compliance for EU customers before publish.
[11:31] Maya Kapoor: We'll flag the EU region note prominently and include a checklist for data residency.
[11:40] [12:00] -- Clarifications on the RA diagram --
[12:00] Diego Ramos: We'll include two RA diagrams: one simplified for the marketplace listing page and one detailed for the engineering runbook. The detailed one will show cert exchange, KMS, and port lists.
[12:15] Priya Singh: For the port lists, customers sometimes freak out at raw ports; maybe present it as a minimal set and an advanced appendix.
[12:24] Diego Ramos: Yep, minimal in the main doc, advanced in appendix.
[12:28] [13:00] -- Live notes & small stumbles --
[13:00] Liam O'Neill: Apologies, just a sec — connection jitter.
[13:06] Priya Singh: No worries, all good.
[13:09] Diego Ramos: Quick note — we also support webhooks for provisioning callbacks; we'll include sample curl examples.
[13:16] [14:00] -- Action item recap --
[14:00] Avery Chen: Recap — Redwood: RA draft, SOC2/comp pack, benchmark runbook, provisioning API sample, demo video outline. OrionCloud: assets, legal checklist, review window, SAML metadata. We'll send calendar invites for the benchmark runs.
[14:18] Markus Vogel: Good, we'll aim to review RA by the 23rd.
[14:22] Priya Singh: I'll prepare the logos and demo script.
[14:25] [14:40] -- Closing --
[14:40] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the RA draft and a shared Google drive link. Expect the RA and asset template in the follow-up email.
[14:50] Liam O'Neill: Thanks all.
[14:52] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[14:53] Diego Ramos: Thanks, bye.
[14:55] Maya Kapoor: Bye.
[15:00] -- end of recording --
